plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero for capital preservation.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small allocations.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to address concentration and its below-stop status.
This approach balances risk and growth by reducing overall leverage and concentration.
It maintains some exposure to growth while prioritizing risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for a more stable growth trajectory. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a blend of broad market and quality tech exposure.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to address concentration and its below-stop status.
Buy TSLA, VRT, and SQQQ at 5% each, leveraging strong scanner long setups.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs SOXL, MUU, and MSFU to 6% each.
This plan aggressively leans into high-scoring setups and increased leverage.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring scanner setups. Be aware of substantially higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) and high-beta METU to zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income focus.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income-focused ETFs and cutting high-beta/leveraged positions. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in selloffs, and distributions are variable.
